clue.text: Good driving is an asset going round it

definitions.text: Good driving is an asset going round it

parts.words: Good driving is an asset going round it
parts.note: reads like advice for motorists on a ring road, but the driving is with a club off the tee and going round means playing all eighteen holes

explanation.walkthrough: The motoring picture misleads: a drive in golf is the long opening shot, so good driving helps you get round the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Players travel around a set of holes on the links, where long drives off the tee help a lot.

clue.text: Weather protection for morning doctor's round

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are placed round, enclosing, the morning abbreviation

parts.note: GP, a general practitioner, is a family doctor
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A GP setting out on a morning round takes rain protection.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAMP is an old British word for a large umbrella, after Mrs Gamp in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella shields you from the rain, so it is protection against the weather.

clue.text: What a 100-Watt 2-volt bulb produces

parts.note: the electrical specs describe a household bulb, and what any such bulb gives off is the glow of a lamp

explanation.walkthrough: The '2' points to this very entry, so the clue describes the output of its own answer's bulb; there is no further wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb fitted in a household lamp gives illumination, the glow such a fitting casts.

clue.text: Draw up a daily telegraph leader

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from telegraph

explanation.surface: An instruction to compose the main editorial column for the Daily Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Telegraph' looks like the newspaper's name; split it: a daily is a CHAR (British for a cleaner) and the telegraph's leader is its first letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out or plot something, such as a course or graph, is to set it down as a diagram.

clue.text: Fabulous supporter of royalty

parts.note: fabulous means mythical, out of fable, and a supporter is a heraldic figure holding up the royal coat of arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a loyal fan of the monarchy; in heraldry it is a beast flanking a shield. The British royal arms have a lion and this one-horned creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned mythical horse stands on the Scottish side of the British royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Performer of high note

parts.note: of high note seems to mean a famous artist, but read literally it is a singer whose notes are high

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of high note' sounds like 'of great renown'; the clue really means a singer who takes the highest vocal part.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice belongs to a vocalist who reaches the top notes.

clue.text: Bath the setting for this opera?

definitions.text: Bath the setting for this opera?

parts.words: Bath the setting for this opera?
parts.note: Bath suggests the Georgian city as a stage setting, but a bathtub is where a cleansing bar is found, and the bar names a kind of TV drama

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city, so an opera set there sounds plausible; really a bath is where you use this, and a TV serial drama is a ___ opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning bar used in the tub also names the long-running television serial, the ___ opera.

clue.text: Attack! Throw a stone!

indicators.note: to throw something is to toss it about, so the letters of stone are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A battle cry ordering troops to charge and hurl rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw a stone' reads as an order; 'Throw' is the anagram signal on STONE, and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault or the beginning of an offensive is an onrush against the enemy.

clue.text: Lacking inspiration, he goes for a walk

explanation.definitionFit: Dull and uninspired prose is plodding, and a person travelling on foot rather than by car is a walker.

clue.text: Breaking into a politician's address

parts.note: breaking into an address sounds like burgling a house, but here it means interrupting a speech with shouted jibes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a home to burgle; it is a speech, and breaking into it means shouting interruptions from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting jeers and interruptions during a public speech is a heckler's activity.

clue.text: It's poisonous so mother gets a doctor in

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go in, between the mother and the article

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree used for a doctor

explanation.surface: Something toxic means mum calls in a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: This African snake has a venomous bite, so it is a toxic creature.

clue.text: Forced into service — and unlikely to forget it

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors were once conscripted by press gangs, and someone strongly struck by an event keeps a lasting memory of it.

clue.text: Large amount of the polar variety

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of the polar appear in a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of the kind of thing found near the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess or glut is a superabundance, far more than is needed.

clue.text: They fly — one type is self-controlled

definitions.text: They fly — one type is self-controlled

parts.words: They fly — one type is self-controlled
parts.note: toys on strings fly under a child's control, while the bird of prey of the same name flies under its own control

explanation.walkthrough: The toy flies on a string held by someone else; the bird of prey sharing its name controls itself in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper toys on strings and hawk-like birds of prey both soar in the air.

clue.text: The lager to change to, on the whole

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the lager to are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that, all things considered, this beer is the one to switch to.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'to' is a link word; the fodder is THE LAGER TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a whole, in total or overall, everything considered together.

clue.text: Discover, though not in the dark apparently

explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something is to find it by chance, and a bulb switched on means the room is illuminated.

clue.text: Ring fighter

parts.note: ring suggests a boxing ring, but here it is the bullring, where a fighter faces the bull

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring fighter' sounds like a boxer; the ring is a Spanish bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter, especially a mounted one, battles bulls in the arena.

clue.text: Famous actor, one seen in a musical

indicators.note: the single letter is seen in, placed inside, the title of the show

parts.note: OLIVER! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor appears in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was one of the great English stage and screen actors of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English Shakespearean actor of stage and screen.

clue.text: Sixth sense needed in teaching

parts.note: taken as written
tuition means instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: Teachers need a sixth sense to manage a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinctive knowledge without reasoning is often called a hunch or gut feeling.

clue.text: Rock formation off-cut

parts.note: out means off, as in a light turned off
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A piece of rock formation that has been cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock jutting above the soil surface is a visible exposed mass of stone.

clue.text: A charge made by river boards

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
the boards is a name for the theatre stage

explanation.surface: A fee made by those on a river authority's boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boards' looks like committees; it is the stage, as in 'treading the boards'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee for sending a letter or parcel is a mailing cost.

clue.text: A target set out for meeting between banks

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of a target are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A goal is fixed for a meeting between banking firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggest financial institutions; they are river banks, and the meeting is a boat race event.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of boat races held on a river is a rowing meet between the two banks.

clue.text: Neat combination of cardinal and count

parts.note: cardinal red is a vivid scarlet, the colour of a cardinal's robes
a poll is a count of votes or heads

explanation.surface: A tidy blend of a cardinal and a count, two church and noble titles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy'; it is an old word for cattle, and the Red Poll is a British breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, and the Red Poll is a hornless red breed of them.

clue.text: Small part actor in a fortuitous run

explanation.definitionFit: A film walk-on is played by a background performer, and in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye, is a bonus one.

clue.text: Infant raised to do simple arithmetic

parts.note: a tot is a small child
up means raised, as a hand held up

explanation.surface: A small child is brought up to do basic sums.
explanation.definitionFit: To add numbers together for a total is basic sum work.

clue.text: Spin, slide and skid

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft or car slewing sideways out of control is slipping laterally, a skid, slide or spin.

clue.text: Seafood starter, something to chew

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, here the first of seafood

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco

explanation.surface: A restaurant dish of seafood served first, a chewy morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: calamari is a seafood starter, notoriously chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: This tentacled cephalopod, fried as calamari, is a chewy seafood dish often served first.

clue.text: Like to get a first-class return for the continent

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class

explanation.surface: Wanting a first-class return ticket for a trip to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The continent' in British usage means mainland Europe; here it is the largest continent. A1 for first-class is written AI in crosswords, so reversed it gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest landmass, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific, is one of the seven continents.

clue.text: Top hat too fancy? It's a controversial issue

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at elaborate reworking, so the letters of top hat too are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a top hat is too fancy, a touchy question of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate topic nobody wants to handle is like something too scalding to hold.

clue.text: Can be turned into American kitchen cabinets

indicators.note: the turned can goes into the abbreviation for American

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

indicators.note: turned means the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A can may become American kitchen cupboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes NIT from TIN, and 'into' puts it inside US.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted kitchen cupboards are sold as modular pieces, each one a separate module.

clue.text: Fasten a string of pearls

explanation.definitionFit: To tie something up with cord is to secure it, and a long necklace of pearls is called a rope.

clue.text: Poison a beautiful Italian girl

explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a toxic plant, and in Italian bella donna means a lovely lady.
